bank.name: Plain and Ordinary Meaning
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the element's terminology is facially clear and has a definitive, ordinary meaning to a person of ordinary skill in the art without requiring external context. Score lower if terms are inherently subjective or ambiguous.

bank.name: Internal Logical Consistency
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the text is completely self-contained, logically coherent, and free from internal contradictions or obscure phrasing. Score lower if limitations, ranges, or descriptions within the isolated text conflict with one another.

bank.name: Grammatical and Syntactic Coherence
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the text uses correct grammar, punctuation, and clear syntax to unambiguously link modifiers to the correct nouns. Score lower if poor grammar or awkward literal translations obscure the metes and bounds.

bank.name: Relative Terminology and Terms of Degree
bank.instruction: Score 10 if relative terms or terms of degree (e.g., 'substantially', 'about') provide an objective baseline or standard for measurement within the text. Score lower if such terms lack discernible boundaries.

bank.name: Antecedent Basis Integrity
bank.instruction: Score 10 if every introduced noun or component properly transitions from an indefinite article ('a' or 'an') to definite references ('said' or 'the') without losing logical linkage. Score lower if prior references are missing or improperly formed.

bank.name: Prepositional and Relational Clarity
bank.instruction: Score 10 if spatial, physical, or logical prepositions (e.g., 'on', 'to', 'attached to') clearly and precisely define the relationships between components. Score lower if relational terms are missing or ambiguous.

bank.name: Negative Limitation Clarity
bank.instruction: Score 10 if any exclusions or disclaimers (e.g., 'free of', 'other than') clearly and unambiguously define the boundaries of what is excluded. Score lower if negative limitations are vague or confusing.

bank.name: Numerical Range Definiteness
bank.instruction: Score 10 if numerical ranges and parameters are clearly bounded, mathematically clear, and free from overlapping or open-ended indefiniteness (e.g., 'up to 50% or more'). Score lower if ranges are contradictory or unconstrained.

bank.name: Parameter Measurement Completeness
bank.instruction: Score 10 if non-standard parameters or mathematical relationships recited in the text intrinsically define the method or units required to measure them. Score lower if measurement methodology is omitted, rendering the parameter scope unascertainable.

bank.name: Vague Modifiers Avoidance
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the text is free of inherently imprecise modifiers or unbounded experimental phrasing. Score lower if it relies on vague modifiers (e.g., 'high quality', 'optimized') that fail to delineate technological scope.

bank.name: Statutory Category Compliance
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the text clearly and cleanly defines an element that unambiguously falls within a single proper statutory category (process, machine, manufacture, or composition). Score lower if it confusingly mixes categories or claims a non-statutory concept.

bank.name: Mental Process Exclusion
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the element recites concrete physical acts or specific hardware so that it cannot be performed purely as a human mental step. Score lower if the text captures purely cognitive actions or abstract mental processes.

bank.name: Abstract Idea Integration
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the text recites specific structural or active steps that integrate a judicial exception into a concrete, practical application. Score lower if it merely recites an abstract idea or fundamental concept.

bank.name: Natural Phenomenon Distinction
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the text explicitly limits a nature-based product with markedly different characteristics from its naturally occurring counterpart. Score lower if it attempts to claim a naturally occurring product without human intervention.

bank.name: Mathematical Concept Constraint
bank.instruction: Score 10 if recited mathematical formulas or relationships are structurally tied to a specific practical application. Score lower if the text attempts to monopolize a standalone mathematical principle or bare algorithm.

bank.name: Inventive Concept Specificity
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the text recites specific technical details or meaningful limitations that amount to significantly more than a mere recitation of a judicial exception. Score lower if it simply instructs to 'apply it' on a generic computer.

bank.name: Specific Structural Recitation
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the element defines the invention by concrete physical structure, exact materials, or specific mechanical components. Score lower if it relies entirely on conceptual generalizations without structural detail.

bank.name: Functional vs. Structural Claiming
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the text recites specific hardware or structural boundaries performing a function. Score lower if it relies exclusively on functional language (what it does) rather than defining what the component physically is.

bank.name: Means-Plus-Function Triggering
bank.instruction: Score 10 if generic functional placeholders (e.g., 'means for') intentionally invoke statutory means-plus-function interpretation, or if clear structure avoids this interpretation entirely. Score lower if ambiguous functional language inadvertently triggers it.

bank.name: Result-Oriented Claiming
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the element recites concrete step-by-step methodologies or mechanical actions. Score lower if it attempts to monopolize a desired outcome or solution without detailing the specific means used to accomplish it.

bank.name: Technical Improvement Specificity
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the text articulates a specific technological solution or improvement to computer functionality. Score lower if it merely recites a desired functional result using generic computer components.

bank.name: Intended Use Limitation
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the element clearly defines structural or active limitations rather than relying merely on intended use or purpose statements. Score lower if it attempts to distinguish prior art solely based on a newly discovered result or field of use.

bank.name: Proper Transitional Phrasing
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the element uses a clear, legally recognized transitional phrase (e.g., 'comprising', 'consisting of') to unambiguously define the boundaries as open, partially open, or closed. Score lower if transitional phrasing is missing or unclear.

bank.name: Markush Group Formatting
bank.instruction: Score 10 if a group of alternatives is presented cohesively using proper closed syntax (e.g., 'selected from the group consisting of'). Score lower if alternative groupings lack proper closure or structural coherence.

bank.name: Closed Group Species Coherence
bank.instruction: Score 10 if species presented in a closed grouping clearly share a common structural property, ensuring all members will actually serve the claimed purpose. Score lower if the grouping improperly mixes unrelated materials or abstract concepts.

bank.name: Dependent Claim Syntax
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the element properly links to a prior claim in the alternative to narrow its scope, without serving as a basis for another multiple dependent claim. Score lower if it improperly refers to multiple distinct claims cumulatively.

bank.name: Preamble Structural Linkage
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the body of the element relates to and is structurally bounded by the context set forth in the claim's preamble. Score lower if the preamble is ignored or if the body lacks necessary context from it.

bank.name: Jepson Claim Separation
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the text clearly structures a preamble as prior art and distinctly separates claimed novel improvements in the body. Score lower if the distinction between known features and novel additions is textually blurred.

bank.name: Product-by-Process Specificity
bank.instruction: Score 10 if a product-by-process limitation textually defines properties that make the resulting product distinguishable from prior art. Score lower if the limitation merely recites manufacturing steps without defining the product itself.

bank.name: Patent Profanity Avoidance
bank.instruction: Score 10 if the text avoids absolute or unintentionally limiting language (e.g., 'must', 'always', 'critical'). Score lower if such terms inadvertently narrow the scope of the claim element.
